name: Khöömii (Mongolian overtone singing)
lineage: Mongolian throat-singing overtone-vocal-technique tradition, the canonical method of simultaneous fundamental-and-formant-overtone production via aryepiglottic-fold steppe-narrowing of the throat. Eight named sub-techniques: kharkhiraa deep-low-fundamental-with-loud-overtones, sygyt high-melodic-overtone-isolation, ezengileer rhythmic-jaw-vibration, dumchuktaar nasal-passage technique, shahaa fluttering-overtone-modulation, khoomei middle-register basic-style, bagalzuuryn-khoomei smooth-style, and khamryn-khoomei nostril-and-mouth combined-resonance. Practiced traditionally by Western-Mongolian Khalkha-Oirat herder communities, contextualized within nomadic-pastoralist horse-and-livestock work-song repertoire and shamanic-spirit-communication ritual.
